historical_references.reference: Ibn Battuta, a famous Moroccan traveler, visited Patan in 1335 CE during his travels in India. He described it as a prosperous city and the center of Gujarat's trade.

The name 'Patan' is believed to have originated from the Sanskrit word 'Pataliputra', meaning 'City of the Underworld'. Patan was the capital city of the Gujarat Sultanate in medieval India, and was later ruled by the Mughals and the Marathas.
